content.title: ‘Harry Potter’ Special ‘Finding Harry’ Is New On Streaming This Weekend
content.text: Finding Harry: The Craft Behind the Magic" key artHBOFinding Harry: The Craft Behind the Magic, a special about the making of the new Harry Potter TV series, is new on streaming and cable.HBO began generating the excitement for Season 1 of the Harry Potter series on March 26, when it released the trailer for the first set of episodes that are based on author J.K Rowling’s worldwide bestseller Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone.ForbesHasbro To Create ‘Harry Potter’ Dolls, Action Figures For TV SeriesNow a week later, HBO Max is going to keep the train rolling to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry with a behind-the-scenes look at the series with Finding Harry: The Craft Behind the Magic,debuted on Sunday at 3 p.m. ET/12 p.m. PT in the U.S. and 8 p.m. in the U.K.The special will also premiere on HBO on cable at 8 p.m. ET/PT on Sunday.For viewers who don’t subscribe to HBO Max, streaming platform has an ad-based subscription costs $9.99 per month, as well as an ad-free subscription for $16.99 per month. HBO Max also offers an ad-free tier with 4K Ultra HD programming for $20.99 per month.What Will Be Featured In ‘Finding Harry: The Craft Behind The Magic’?According to HBO, Finding Harry: The Craft Behind the Magic will offer “an inside look at the epic scale and meticulous care” behind the Harry Potter series. The special will include a look at the extensive search that resulted in the casting of Harry Potter, Hermione Granger and Ron Weasley — played by Dominic McLaughlin, Arabella Stanton and Alastair Stout, respectively — as well as interviews with members of the casting, production design, costume design and creature effects crews.In addition, Finding Harry: The Craft Behind the Magic will include interviews with John Lithgow (Albus Dumbledore), Janet McTeer (Minerva McGonagall), Paapa Essiedu (Severus Snape) and Nick Frost (Rubeus Hagrid), who will also narrate the special. The first season of Harry Potter will be released in December and consist of eight episodes. The debut of the series comes 25 years after the release of the first of eight Harry Potter films, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone, which starred Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint as Harry, Ron and Hermione.The Harry Potter film series wrapped up in 2011 with the release of Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows Part 2.Finding Harry: The Craft Behind the Magic began streaming on HBO Max on Sunday at 3 p.m. ET/12 p.m. PT and will debut on cable on HBO at 8 p.m. ET/PT.Forbes‘Beetlejuice’ Action Figure Of Winona Ryder’s Lydia Deetz Is In The WorksBy Tim Lammers
